Rater Handbook: Holistic Judgement
Revised 10 October 2026 (B.E. 2569)
For raters

You are an independent rater in a study of corporate sustainability disclosure. You will receive a blinded workbook containing claims from sustainability reports, passages from the same report that relate to each claim, and columns for recording your judgement.

You do not need prior knowledge of any instrument or scoring criteria, and we ask you not to study other criteria while you are rating. What this study needs is your judgement as a reader of the report.
1. What you are judging

In each row, please judge one thing only: does this report give enough information to check or question this claim? Please judge from the point of view of a reader who wants to check this claim or hold the company to it. Examples of such readers are analysts or investors, assurers, regulators, civil society organisations or the media, and lenders. Do not judge from the point of view of a general reader who only skims the report.
2. Principles of judgement

2.1 Judge the claim, not the organisation. You do not need to consider whether the claim is true, whether the company actually did it, or whether the company contributes to any SDG. A claim may be fully supported in the report and still be false (written but not done). Conversely, a true claim may have no supporting information in the report (done but not written). The judgement therefore rests only on what the report discloses.

2.2 Read only the information given in the workbook. Do not use outside evidence (for example news, ratings, or personal knowledge of the company). If you happen to know something about the company, please do not use it in your judgement.
2.3 Do not judge intent. Words such as symbolic, greenwashing, over-claiming and under-claiming describe behaviour; they are not judgements and should not be written in the notes column.
3. What you receive for each claim
Each row in the workbook is one claim. A claim is one sentence or one bullet point that states an action, target, result or status related to the SDGs. Each row contains the following:

Note: Passages 1 to 5 are the output of a retrieval tool. They may be incomplete and vary in relevance. Please judge from the information given only. Where no passage is given, the cell shows "(no passage retrieved)". This is information about that report, not a retrieval error.
4. Holistic judgement
Please follow these steps, in order, for each row.
4.1 Read the claim and supporting passages 1 to 5.
4.2 Choose your judgement from the three levels below.
Please write the criteria, keywords or method you use for each level in the right-hand column, so that we understand your view of Unsubstantiated, Partially substantiated and Substantiated.

Once you have used these criteria to rate, do not go back and change them. If you want to change them, write in the Note area below the table why, or at what point, you changed your mind about the criteria you first wrote.
For this judgement, please use your own judgement as to whether the information given is "enough" for the readers described in Section 1.

4.3 Record in what_made_you_decide what led you to your judgement. Use short words or phrases, not paragraphs, for example "has figures but does not say how they were measured" or "only a statement, nothing to check". (Note: you may write a summary of your criteria as a whole; you do not need to write one for each claim, unless you have an important note about a particular claim.)

4.4 When you have judged every row, please write a closing note in the "Closing notes" box at the end of the table: overall, what approach or method did you use to judge, and did it change while you worked, and if so, how?
5. Rules
Judge the rows in the order they appear in the file. Do not sort or filter rows.

Judge each row once only. Do not go back to "adjust" an earlier row after rating other rows. If you feel your standard has changed, record this in what_made_you_decide at the row where you noticed it, continue to the end, and summarise it again in the closing note.

If you hesitate between two levels (for example Partially substantiated and Substantiated), choose the level you think is closest and record your hesitation in what_made_you_decide. Do not leave the judgement blank.
Add a note when the claim text is incomplete or cannot be understood.
Do not describe the organisation's behaviour, for example that the organisation is greenwashing.
Do not edit locked columns.
Do not discuss with other raters until you have returned your workbook.
6. How your judgements will be used

Your judgements will be compared with the results of another group of raters who rated the same claims with a different method, to test whether that method reflects the understanding of real readers. For this reason, it is essential that you use your own judgement without knowing the other group's criteria. The research team will explain the other group's method to you after you have returned your work.
